content: To see what is right and not do it is a lack of courage.
author: Confucius
story:
Living through the violent chaos and moral fragmentation of the Spring and Autumn period in ancient China, Confucius wandered between feudal states offering counsel to self-serving warlords who repeatedly dismissed him. Undeterred, he gathered devoted disciples to restore societal harmony not through force, but through personal integrity, ritual propriety (Li), filial reverence, and human-heartedness (Ren).

In formulating this reflection, Confucius stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of courage. For Confucius, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
